### Simple Bubble Chart

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

data <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/school_earnings.csv")

data |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~Women,
    y = ~Men,
    text = ~School,
    mode = "markers",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(size = ~Gap, opacity = 0.5)
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Gender Gap in Earnings per University",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(showgrid = FALSE),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(showgrid = FALSE)
  )
```

### Setting Multiple Colors

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

data <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/school_earnings.csv")

colors <- c('rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(222,45,38,0.8)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)',
            'rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)',
            'rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)',
            'rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)', 'rgba(204,204,204,1)',
            'rgba(204,204,204,1)')
# Note: The colors will be assigned to each observations based on the order of the observations in the dataframe.

data |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~Women,
    y = ~Men,
    text = ~School,
    mode = "markers",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(size = ~Gap, opacity = 0.5, color = colors)
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Gender Gap in Earnings per University",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(showgrid = FALSE),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(showgrid = FALSE)
  )
```

### Mapping a Color Variable (Continuous)

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

data <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/school_earnings.csv")

data |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~Women,
    y = ~Men,
    text = ~School,
    mode = "markers",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      size = ~Gap,
      opacity = 0.5,
      color = ~Gap,
      colorscale = "Reds",
      showscale = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Gender Gap in Earnings per University",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(showgrid = FALSE),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(showgrid = FALSE)
  )
```

### Mapping a Color Variable (Categorical)

Map `marker.color` to a categorical column to get one trace per category, coloured from the `colorway`. Here the bubble diameters are rescaled to between 10 and 100 pixels.

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

data <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/school_earnings.csv")

data$State <- as.factor(c('Massachusetts', 'California', 'Massachusetts', 'Pennsylvania', 'New Jersey', 'Illinois', 'Washington DC',
                          'Massachusetts', 'Connecticut', 'New York', 'North Carolina', 'New Hampshire', 'New York', 'Indiana',
                          'New York', 'Michigan', 'Rhode Island', 'California', 'Georgia', 'California', 'California'))

# One color per state, interpolated from the "Paired" palette
state_colors <- colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(12, "Paired"))(nlevels(data$State))
data$size <- scales::rescale(data$Gap, to = c(10, 100))

data |>
  go_figure() |>
  update_layout(colorway = state_colors) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~Women,
    y = ~Men,
    text = ~School,
    mode = "markers",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      size = ~size,
      opacity = 0.5,
      sizemode = "diameter",
      color = ~State
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Gender Gap in Earnings per University",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(showgrid = FALSE),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(showgrid = FALSE),
    showlegend = FALSE
  )
```

### Scaling the Size of Bubble Charts

Choose the range of the bubbles' sizes by rescaling the size variable yourself, here to between 10 and 50 pixels:

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

data <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/school_earnings.csv")

data$State <- as.factor(c('Massachusetts', 'California', 'Massachusetts', 'Pennsylvania', 'New Jersey', 'Illinois', 'Washington DC',
                          'Massachusetts', 'Connecticut', 'New York', 'North Carolina', 'New Hampshire', 'New York', 'Indiana',
                          'New York', 'Michigan', 'Rhode Island', 'California', 'Georgia', 'California', 'California'))

# One color per state, interpolated from the "Paired" palette
state_colors <- colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(12, "Paired"))(nlevels(data$State))
data$size <- scales::rescale(data$Gap, to = c(10, 50))

data |>
  go_figure() |>
  update_layout(colorway = state_colors) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~Women,
    y = ~Men,
    text = ~School,
    mode = "markers",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      size = ~size,
      opacity = 0.5,
      sizemode = "diameter",
      color = ~State
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Gender Gap in Earnings per University",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(showgrid = FALSE),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(showgrid = FALSE),
    showlegend = FALSE
  )
```

### Scaling using Sizeref

To scale the bubble size, use the attribute sizeref. We recommend using the following formula to calculate a sizeref value:<br><br>
sizeref = 2. * max(array of size values) / (desired maximum marker size ** 2)
<br><br>
Note that setting sizeref to a value greater than 1 decreases the rendered marker sizes, while setting sizeref to less than 1 increases the rendered marker sizes. See `go_scatter_marker()` for more information.
<br><br>
Additionally, we recommend setting the sizemode attribute to area.

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

data <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/school_earnings.csv")

data$State <- as.factor(c('Massachusetts', 'California', 'Massachusetts', 'Pennsylvania', 'New Jersey', 'Illinois', 'Washington DC',
                          'Massachusetts', 'Connecticut', 'New York', 'North Carolina', 'New Hampshire', 'New York', 'Indiana',
                          'New York', 'Michigan', 'Rhode Island', 'California', 'Georgia', 'California', 'California'))

# One color per state, interpolated from the "Paired" palette
state_colors <- colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(12, "Paired"))(nlevels(data$State))

#Use the ideal sizeref value
desired_maximum_marker_size <- 40
your_list_of_size_values <- data['Gap']
sizeref <- 2.0 * max(your_list_of_size_values) / (desired_maximum_marker_size**2)

data |>
  go_figure() |>
  update_layout(colorway = state_colors) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~Women,
    y = ~Men,
    text = ~School,
    mode = "markers",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      size = ~Gap,
      opacity = 0.5,
      sizemode = "area",
      sizeref = sizeref,
      color = ~State
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Gender Gap in Earnings per University",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(showgrid = FALSE),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(showgrid = FALSE),
    showlegend = FALSE
  )
```

### Hover Text with Bubble Charts

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

data <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/school_earnings.csv")

data$State <- as.factor(c('Massachusetts', 'California', 'Massachusetts', 'Pennsylvania', 'New Jersey', 'Illinois', 'Washington DC',
                          'Massachusetts', 'Connecticut', 'New York', 'North Carolina', 'New Hampshire', 'New York', 'Indiana',
                          'New York', 'Michigan', 'Rhode Island', 'California', 'Georgia', 'California', 'California'))

# One color per state, interpolated from the "Paired" palette
state_colors <- colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(12, "Paired"))(nlevels(data$State))
data$size <- scales::rescale(data$Gap, to = c(10, 50))

data |>
  go_figure() |>
  update_layout(colorway = state_colors) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~Women,
    y = ~Men,
    text = ~ paste("School:", School, "<br>Gender Gap:", Gap),
    mode = "markers",
    hoverinfo = "text",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      size = ~size,
      opacity = 0.5,
      sizemode = "diameter",
      color = ~State
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Gender Gap in Earnings per University",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(showgrid = FALSE),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(showgrid = FALSE),
    showlegend = FALSE
  )
```

### Styled Buble Chart

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

data <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/gapminderDataFiveYear.csv")

data_2007 <- data[which(data$year == 2007),]
data_2007 <- data_2007[order(data_2007$continent, data_2007$country),]
slope <- 2.666051223553066e-05
data_2007$size <- sqrt(data_2007$pop * slope)
colors <- c('#4AC6B7', '#1972A4', '#965F8A', '#FF7070', '#C61951')

data_2007 |>
  go_figure() |>
  update_layout(colorway = colors) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~gdpPercap,
    y = ~lifeExp,
    mode = "markers",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      size = ~size,
      color = ~continent,
      symbol = "circle",
      sizemode = "diameter",
      line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 2, color = "#FFFFFF")
    ),
    text = ~ paste(
      "Country:", country,
      "<br>Life Expectancy:", lifeExp,
      "<br>GDP:", gdpPercap,
      "<br>Pop.:", pop
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Life Expectancy v. Per Capita GDP, 2007",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(
      title = "GDP per capita (2000 dollars)",
      gridcolor = "rgb(255, 255, 255)",
      range = c(2.003297660701705, 5.191505530708712),
      type = "log",
      zerolinewidth = 1,
      ticklen = 5,
      gridwidth = 2
    ),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(
      title = "Life Expectancy (years)",
      gridcolor = "rgb(255, 255, 255)",
      range = c(36.12621671352166, 91.72921793264332),
      zerolinewidth = 1,
      ticklen = 5,
      gridwidth = 2
    ),
    paper_bgcolor = "rgb(243, 243, 243)",
    plot_bgcolor = "rgb(243, 243, 243)"
  )
```

#Reference

See `go_scatter()` and `go_scatter_marker()` for more information and chart attribute options!
